subject.title: memory-core: silent fallback to full-corpus JSON embedding scan when post-KNN filters exhaust the k=4096 ceiling

question: Should memory-core prioritize bounded gateway latency by returning capped filtered KNN results with explicit recall-clipped diagnostics, or retain a full-recall fallback and fund a different bounded retrieval/storage design?
rationale: Current main intentionally falls back to preserve filtered recall, while the proposed containment changes that observable retrieval contract; selecting the lasting recall-versus-liveness policy and any public diagnostic surface requires maintainer intent.

options.title: Contain and disclose clipped recall
options.body: Stop before the JSON full-corpus scan after the native KNN ceiling and expose a stable diagnostic that tells callers when filters clipped recall.

options.title: Preserve full filtered recall
options.body: Keep a bounded full-recall path only after maintainers choose and prove a retrieval design that cannot monopolize the gateway event loop.

options.title: Plan a storage and index redesign
options.body: Treat BLOB embeddings or sharded/indexed retrieval as a separate migration proposal with explicit compatibility, rollout, and benchmark evidence.

recommendation.title: Contain and disclose clipped recall
recommendation.body: Stop before the JSON full-corpus scan after the native KNN ceiling and expose a stable diagnostic that tells callers when filters clipped recall.

likelyOwner.reason: They supplied the production measurements and concrete contract tradeoff, though their decision-owner status is not established from repository history.
